title: Nonlinear Response via Sublinear Optics
authors: Mykhaylo Khoma, Valeriia Bilokon, Elvira Bilokon, Denys I. Bondar
abstract: Sublinear optical response, in which the emitted field scales as a fractional power of the driving field, lies beyond the conventional perturbative hierarchy of nonlinear optics. Here, we show that such a response can be engineered in a hydrogen atom using tracking control. Rather than prescribing the driving waveform, the field is determined self-consistently from the evolving quantum state to enforce a chosen relation between the optical response and the applied field. We demonstrate accurate tracking for multiple exponents and scaling strengths, establishing that a single atomic system can be driven to realize a family of distinct sublinear responses. The calculations are enabled by a compact wave-packet continuum discretization that treats bound and continuum states on equal footing and is applied here, to the best of our knowledge, for the first time to strong-field optics and quantum control. These results establish tracking control as a general route to engineering optical responses beyond conventional polynomial nonlinearities.
summary: The paper demonstrates a novel method using tracking control to force an atomic system (hydrogen) into exhibiting sublinear optical response scaling. By self-consistently determining the driving field based on a target power law, they prove that such non-perturbative nonlinearities can be engineered in quantum systems. This establishes tracking control as a general tool for designing exotic light-matter interactions.
main_problem: The research aims to engineer optical responses that exhibit sublinear scaling, which falls outside the standard perturbative framework of nonlinear optics.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate that a quantum system can be driven using tracking control to realize prescribed sublinear optical responses in hydrogen atoms.
method: They employ a self-consistent tracking control loop where the driving field is determined by enforcing a desired relationship between the measured dipole acceleration and the applied field.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a hydrogen atom interacting with an intense, linearly polarized laser field. The calculations utilize a specialized Wave-Packet Continuum Discretization (WPCD) basis that treats both bound and continuum states equally.

why_interesting: This work provides a general theoretical framework—tracking control—to engineer complex optical responses in quantum systems beyond simple polynomial nonlinearities, which is highly relevant for advanced quantum optics and light-matter interaction studies.

figures.caption: FIG. 2. Numerical verification of the Ehrenfest theorems. The left- and right-hand sides of the two Ehrenfest relations, d dt⟨z⟩= ⟨pz⟩+A(t) (top) and d dt⟨p⟩= ⟨Fz⟩(bottom), are com- puted independently from the simulated wave function and plotted as functions of time. The near-perfect overlap of the two curves in each panel indicates that the finite-dimensional representation used here introduces only a negligible violation of the Ehrenfest theorems, confirming the physical reliability of the simulation. See Ref. [45] for computational details.
